newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Lamassoure says dollar still undervalued.
newsitem.headline: France's Lamassoure says dollar still undervalued.

text.p: French government spokesman Alain Lamassoure welcomed on Wednesday the rise of the dollar against European currencies but said it remained undervalued.
"It is true that the dollar is and remains undervalued against the major European currencies," Lamassore told Europe 1 radio.
At the same time, he said, "We must rejoice that in a few days it (the dollar) has gone from five francs to 5.30 francs."
On the French economy, Lamassoure said it was showing clear signs of picking up pace and should start seeing annual growth levels of around 2.5 percent.
There is "a virtual certainty that France will again see growth levels of around 2.5 percent a year (and) that will have a positive impact on jobs and confidence," he said.
"The good news for this autumn is that all the signs point to an acceleration of economic growth," he said.
"The various motors of growth are starting to tick over at high speed," he said, citing stronger household consumption and record exports.
He said business investment, which had been slow in the first half, seemed to be gaining pace in the second half.
The property market, after years of being depressed, also appeared to be improving with new housing sales up 11 percent in the third quarter, he said.
